After three rounds of developer betas, Apple is now rolling out the first public beta of macOS 27. Here's how to install it.

How to install the macOS 27 public beta

As most 9to5Mac readers know, running beta versions of Apple's operating systems means accepting the risk of encountering various bugs, ranging from minor inconveniences to serious issues that could completely brick your device.

That said, the macOS 27 beta has been fairly stable overall, though Safari has experienced occasional performance and memory issues, and some under-the-hood changes have affected the stability of the Spaces feature.

Additionally, as the beta cycle progresses, features that work fine in one build may break in the next, as Apple continues to make major under-the-hood changes. Stability and reliability can vary considerably from beta to beta, so please proceed with extreme caution when installing.

Here's how to install macOS 27 Golden Gate public beta 1:

  • Head to https://beta.apple.com and enrol your Mac in the public beta programme.
  • Go to System Settings → General → Software Update
  • Click the 'i' button next to 'Beta Updates'
  • From the dropdown in the upper right, select 'macOS 27 Golden Gate Public Beta'
  • Click 'Done'

What's new in macOS 27 Golden Gate

This year, the headlining feature across Apple's operating system updates is the new Siri app and a new Siri AI experience. Siri will index content from your Messages, Mail, and other apps so that it can answer questions, execute commands, and more.

As part of Apple's under-the-hood overhaul for Siri AI, macOS 27 Golden Gate also brings major improvements to search. Spotlight search became quite unstable on macOS Tahoe 26, but that issue appears to be largely fixed in macOS 27 Golden Gate. Of course, during the beta period, real-world experience may vary.

Additionally, macOS 27 Golden Gate tweaks the Liquid Glass effect, which many users felt fell short on macOS Tahoe 26. The system also adopts a unified corner radius for windows and apps, meaning the radius of the corners no longer varies based on content and interface elements.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also brings upgrades to Apple Intelligence features, including a redesigned and more efficient Writing Tools suite, enhanced Visual Intelligence capabilities, and a new Safari extension builder that lets you create extensions using natural language prompts.

Shortcuts on macOS 27 Golden Gate gets a similar feature, letting users build shortcuts using prompt-based commands rather than assembling them manually step by step, which some users may find more accessible.

For iPhone Mirroring users, the app now supports more flexible aspect ratios, which many see as Apple's first step toward adapting iPhone apps for a future folding iPhone.
